Then make the terminal answer exactly “Left” or “Right,” or map that side to the displayed option letter and confirm letter/text agree. Trigger: Finalizing a left-versus-right lung abnormality answer after a grounded chest-imaging report, especially when the rationale cites a specific finding from that report.

Observable verification action: Reopen the raw grounded-report observation and locate the exact statement for each lung. Choose a side only if an explicit abnormal finding is attributed to that lung—for example, “3.2 cm nodular density in the left mid-lung”—and the opposite lung is explicitly clear or normal—for example, “the right lung is clear.” Do not treat a non-lung incidental finding such as a left-sided PICC line as proof of lung abnormality. If options are displayed, map the supported side text back to the displayed choice and confirm the letter and text agree; if options are empty, confirm the terminal answer text matches the supported side and that the cited phrase actually appears in the observed report.

Trigger: When finalizing a left/right lung-abnormality answer from a grounded report that gives an anatomical lobe label (for example, “left upper lobe”) plus a bounding box, especially when the question says “in this image” or the allowed answers are simply “left” or “right.”

Observable verification action: Reopen the raw grounded-report finding and its box, then check which laterality convention the question asks for. If the question asks for the side in the image rather than the patient’s anatomical side, map the box center to the displayed image: center x below half the image width = left side of the displayed image; above half = right side. Then make the terminal answer exactly “Left” or “Right,” or map that side to the displayed option letter and confirm letter/text agree. Do not use the report’s anatomical lobe phrase as the side answer. In this case, the observed finding was “Calcified granuloma left upper lobe” with box [670,168,803,322] on a 1024-wide image; that box is on the right half of the displayed image, so the image-side answer is “Right.” The terminal answer instead repeated “left upper lobe …” and lost the requested side. If the question clearly asks anatomical/patient side, use the report’s explicit laterality instead.
